note: Reviewer's returned copy: twelve reworded child hints and three walk scripts written to the house style. Applied verbatim.

hintRewrites.hint: Pick the feeling you can prove using the text. Do not just pick a close match.
When a writer compares two things, they are painting a picture. They are not reporting facts.
Incorrect choices often copy words from the passage. The correct choice explains the idea behind them.
Sometimes the text stays in the middle. Do not rule out options that say 'neither'.
When two answers look very similar, spot the one different word. Check it against the text.
Ask what the text actually tells you. If the text does not say it, avoid it.
Give exactly the number of ticks asked for. An extra tick throws away every mark.
A racing heart usually shows a feeling. Check what the character is feeling right then.
Matching words from the text is not enough. Check that the option answers the question.
For things that happened before the main story, use 'had' plus the verb. Match the tense.
Check what job the word does here. Is it describing a thing or doing the action?
Check the line numbers and re-read just that bit. True facts from other paragraphs are incorrect.

walkScripts.walkScript: Go straight to line 1. It tells you the Mole had been spring-cleaning his little home. That gives you your answer. The other choices happen later in the passage.
The word 'first' is key here. Look for the very first thing the Mole sees. It is 'something bright and small' that twinkles. The face and whiskers appear later.
Look at lines 11 and 12. His answer says he was obliged to be in town the following day. 'Town' means London here. He simply had to be somewhere else.
